info.title: CloudShare API v3
info.description:
The CloudShare REST API v3 (Classic) lets client applications perform a subset of the actions available in the CloudShare web application: creating environments, checking their status, taking snapshots, managing training classes and inviting users.

## Authentication
Every request is signed with your API ID and API Key using the `cs_sha1` HMAC-SHA1 scheme; see the `cs_sha1` security scheme for the algorithm and scripts. OAuth 2.0 tokens from the Accelerate API v4 are not accepted by v3.

In *Try It*, paste a freshly signed header value, including the `cs_sha1 ` prefix, into the `Authorization` field. A header is valid for one call, for the exact URL it was signed for, within a short time window (currently 60 seconds).

## Requests
- All requests must send `Accept: application/json`.
- `PUT` and `POST` requests with a payload must send `Content-Type: application/json`.
- Parameters are passed in the query string, the URL path or the JSON body, as documented for each request.

## Responses
- `204` responses have an empty body.
- Other `2xx` responses return a JSON value (object, array, string, number or boolean).
- `4xx`/`5xx` responses return an `ErrorObject`: `{"message": "User not found", "code": "0x40401"}`. The 3 most significant digits of `code` are the HTTP status code.
- Some endpoints validate the request body and return `400` with a map of field name to error messages instead, e.g. `{"name": ["Name is required."]}`.
- Authentication errors:
  - `401` `0x40101` / `0x40102`: the `Authorization` header is missing, or the signature does not match the URL, API ID or API Key.
  - `403` `0x40303`: the token was already used. Generate a new header for every call.
  - `403` `0x40304`: your account reached its API call limit.
  - `500` `0x50018`: the timestamp is outside the allowed window. Check your clock.
  - `500` `0x50019`: the token is not exactly 10 characters.

## Formats
- Enum values are returned as integers unless documented otherwise.
- Date-time values are returned as RFC 1123 strings, e.g. `Mon, 26 Oct 2026 10:00:00 GMT`.

## Concepts
| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Environment | A group of machines (VMs), storage, networking and infrastructure software. |
| VM / Machine | A single VM within an environment. |
| VM Template | A pre-configured VM that can be added to an environment. |
| Blueprint | A template of an environment holding zero or more snapshots. |
| Snapshot | The state of an environment and its running machines at a point in time. |
| Environment Template | A preconfigured, read-only blueprint supplied by CloudShare. |
| Environment Policy | Limits an environment's total lifetime and its run time before suspension. |
| Project | A set of resources, blueprints and users. Every blueprint, environment and policy belongs to a project. |
| Project Member | A user who can own and use environments and invite other users. |
| End User | A user of an environment. |

post.description:
Creates a unique link that logs a student into a class automatically, skipping the class login page. The link stays valid until it is disabled with POST /class/disablesponsoredlink; calling this again for the same class and student updates the link. The caller needs permission to edit the class; an unknown class returns `403`.

The login can still fail, for example when the class is not open yet, the class is fully booked, or the class does not allow multiple environment activations and the environment already expired. Unfilled required `registrationInfo` fields may show the class login page, unless *Disable forced registration for Class Sponsored Links* is checked in the project's training settings.

Concurrent requests for the same class with `preRegisterStudent=true` can race and overbook the class; serialize them to enforce the student limit.
Disables a class sponsored link created by POST /class/sponsoredlink. To re-enable it, call POST /class/sponsoredlink again with the same class ID and student email.

cs_sha1.description:
CloudShare API v3 uses an HMAC-SHA1 request signature based on OAuth 1. Every request must carry an `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: cs_sha1 userapiid:<API_ID>;timestamp:<TIMESTAMP>;token:<TOKEN>;hmac:<HMAC>
```

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `userapiid` | Your API ID, from your user details page (*Generate API Credentials*). |
| `timestamp` | Request time in seconds since the Unix epoch. A request is valid within a short time window (currently 60 seconds); outside it the call fails with `500` `0x50018`. |
| `token` | A unique, exactly 10-character random alphanumeric string. A token cannot be reused. |
| `hmac` | Lower-case hex SHA1 digest of the concatenation `API_KEY + FULL_URL + TIMESTAMP + TOKEN`. |

`FULL_URL` is the entire request URL including the query string, e.g. `https://use.cloudshare.com/api/v3/envs/actions/suspend?envId=ENXYZ123`.

Bash example:

```bash
API_ID="<ID>"
API_KEY="<KEY>"
URL="https://use.cloudshare.com/api/v3/envs"
TIMESTAMP=$(date +%s)
TOKEN=$(tr -dc A-Za-z0-9 </dev/urandom | head -c 10)
HMAC=$(echo -n $API_KEY$URL$TIMESTAMP$TOKEN | sha1sum | awk '{print $1}')
curl -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Authorization: cs_sha1 userapiid:$API_ID;timestamp:$TIMESTAMP;token:$TOKEN;hmac:$HMAC" $URL
```

Open source SDKs that handle the signing are available on GitHub for C#, JavaScript, Python and Go.

## Using *Try It*

*Try It* cannot compute the signature for you, so you paste a header you signed yourself. Because the signature covers the exact URL, the time and a single-use token, you need a **new header for every call**:

1. In *Try It*, fill in the path and query parameters first, and copy the full request URL it will call (for example `https://use.cloudshare.com/api/v3/envs/actions/getextended?envId=EN5YTkVIYcD6kL9flyAAYyzg2`).
2. Generate the header for that exact URL with one of the scripts below.
3. Paste the printed value, **including the `cs_sha1 ` prefix**, into the `Authorization` field and send within the time window (currently 60 seconds).

If you change any parameter, or send the same request again, generate a new header; a header signed for a different URL fails with `401`, a reused header with `403` (`0x40303`), and a stale header with `500` (`0x50018`).

Bash:

```bash
API_ID="<ID>"; API_KEY="<KEY>"
URL="https://use.cloudshare.com/api/v3/ping"   # the exact URL Try It will call
TIMESTAMP=$(date +%s)
TOKEN=$(tr -dc A-Za-z0-9 </dev/urandom | head -c 10)
HMAC=$(echo -n "$API_KEY$URL$TIMESTAMP$TOKEN" | sha1sum | awk '{print $1}')
echo "cs_sha1 userapiid:$API_ID;timestamp:$TIMESTAMP;token:$TOKEN;hmac:$HMAC"
```

PowerShell:

```powershell
$ApiId = "<ID>"; $ApiKey = "<KEY>"
$Url = "https://use.cloudshare.com/api/v3/ping"   # the exact URL Try It will call
$Timestamp = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds()
$Token = -join ((48..57) + (65..90) + (97..122) | Get-Random -Count 10 | ForEach-Object { [char]$_ })
$Bytes = [System.Security.Cryptography.SHA1]::Create().ComputeHash([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes("$ApiKey$Url$Timestamp$Token"))
$Hmac = -join ($Bytes | ForEach-Object { $_.ToString("x2") })
"cs_sha1 userapiid:$ApiId;timestamp:$Timestamp;token:$Token;hmac:$Hmac"
```

OAuth 2.0 tokens from the Accelerate API v4 (`/v4/oauth/token`) are **not** accepted by API v3.
